prompt_text: I need a hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t safely look up current local companies from here, but I can tell you exactly which specific kinds of contractors to call in Miami, why each matters for a hurricane-rated replacement, and give a short phone script and checklist so you can quickly vet and hire the best crew. If you give me your zip code or neighborhood I’ll prepare a targeted short list of nearby certified contractors for you to call (you can paste their names back here and I’ll help rank them).

Who to call (and why)
- A GAF Master Elite contractor in Miami
  - Why: Master Elite is GAF’s top installer program (stricter vetting, insurance and warranty requirements). GAF offers WindProven™ and enhanced warranties for high-wind installations.
- An Owens Corning Platinum Preferred contractor in Miami
  - Why: Platinum Preferred contractors qualify for Owens Corning’s best warranties and have training in their impact- and wind-rated systems.
- A CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster (or Landmark PRO installer)
  - Why: CertainTeed’s Select ShingleMasters are trained on their impact-rated shingles and offer strong manufacturer-backed warranties.
- At least one Miami‑Dade County NOA‑listed installer / product specialist
  - Why: For hurricane-prone areas you want products and installation methods that meet Miami‑Dade County or Florida Product Approval (NOA) standards — those are tested for impact and wind uplift.
- A local roofer with proven experience doing hurricane retrofits and wind mitigation retrofits
  - Why: Local experience with Miami building code, permitting, Miami-Dade inspections, and typical construction details (deck attachment, straps, secondary barriers) matters a lot.
- (If you have a large or complex roof) a licensed structural engineer or company that coordinates engineered uplift connections and permits
  - Why: Some roofs (older homes, complex rafters) need engineered details to meet code for high wind loads.

What to ask on the first call (quick vetting checklist)
- Are you licensed in Florida and insured? Can you give license number and insurance certificate?
- Do you install products that meet Florida Product Approval / Miami‑Dade NOA? Which products and NOA numbers?
- Are you a GAF Master Elite / Owens Corning Platinum / CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster (or other) installer? Proof?
- What wind rating will the system meet (mph)? Will you install a Class 4 impact-rated shingle if needed?
- Will you install a secondary water barrier and upgraded roof deck attachment (nail pattern, ring-shank nails, straps)?
- Do you pull permits and coordinate inspections with Miami‑Dade? Who handles HOA approvals?
- What warranties do you offer (manufacturer’s and workmanship)? Are workmanship warranties transferable?
- Can you provide three recent references in Miami with similar homes (same roof slope/size)?
- Do you provide a written estimate with line items (tear-off, underlayment, flashing, straps, permits, disposal)?

Red flags to avoid
- No local license or insurance or refusing to provide license numbers
- No permits, or “cash” only deals that avoid permits
- Very low bids that skip underlayment, deck fasteners, flashing, or secondary barriers
- No references or no Miami jobs in last 12 months

What systems/features to insist on for hurricane resistance
- Products with Florida Product Approval / Miami‑Dade NOA and Class 4 impact rating if you’re in coastal exposure
- Full tear-off (if rot or multiple shingle layers exist) or engineered re-cover per code
- Proper deck attachment (specified nail pattern or screws), hurricane straps/ties, and continuous blocking where needed
- High-quality synthetic underlayment and a secondary water barrier (self-adhered membrane at eaves and any vulnerable areas)
- Metal flashing details, ridge vents rated for high winds, and sealed penetrations
- Written wind speed rating and warranty coverage in the contract

Phone script (short)
“Hi — I need a full roof replacement for a home in [neighborhood/zip]. Are you licensed in Florida and insured? Do you install products that meet Miami‑Dade/Florida Product Approval (NOA)? Are you a [GAF Master Elite / Owens Corning Platinum / CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster]? Will you obtain permits, install a secondary water barrier, and build the system to a [specify desired wind rating] mph standard? Can you give a written estimate and three local references?”

Next step I can do for you
- If you give your zip code or address I’ll list 3–5 nearby certified contractors you should call (you can paste the names back here and I’ll help prioritize).
- Or I can draft a comparison table template you can use to compare estimates and warranties.

Which would you like me to do next — give nearby names (please provide zip) or a printable comparison checklist?
